# Secretary

[English](README.md) | [日本語](README.ja.md) | [Français](README.fr.md) | [中文](README.zh-CN.md)

<!-- Generated by npm run docs:localize; edit docs/i18n/translations.json. -->

Secretary is a persistent personal assistant for Master. Core maintains the main session and working memory, schedules tasks for execution agents or registered programs, and returns their results to the main session. History search, scheduled wakeups, and push notifications support ongoing work. The project pins Pi v0.87.0 and exposes a local Core API v1.

<a id="快速开始"></a>

## Quick start

Requires Node.js ≥22.19, npm, and Python 3. World and history search use PostgreSQL.

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
npm ci
npm start
npm run core -- status
npm run core -- attach
npm run stop
```

Core runs in the background with the fixture model and `.demo-data` as its default data directory. See the [operations guide](docs/en/operations.md) for live models, database setup, backups, and administration. Run `npm run verify` for development checks; see [development checks](docs/en/operations.md#development-checks) for the full PostgreSQL setup.

<a id="开发路线"></a>

## Roadmap

Core now includes an independent lifecycle, reliable sync, Scopes, authorization and resolution of unknown outcomes, model retries, memory search and removal of original inputs from context, scheduled wakeups, proactive push delivery, storage performance improvements, module separation, and reorganized prompts. The current documentation was aligned with the code in [#27](https://github.com/ExplodeCode6324/Secretary/issues/27); see [#7](https://github.com/ExplodeCode6324/Secretary/issues/7) for the overall roadmap.

The current client route follows the [TUI requirements](docs/tui/requirements-and-backend-plan.md). The Tauri/Svelte client is retired; the local browser command interface is documented in [the guide](docs/tui/browser-guide.md). Use the [Core operations guide](docs/en/operations.md). Unfinished GUI acceptance retains its original status.

Device issues #6/#11–#14 remain frozen. SwiftUI is retired; its design is historical only.
